question: Should outbound recovery keep ambiguous post-send entries pending with backoff when no reconciliation-capable adapter is available, instead of allowing them to become terminal failed entries after retry exhaustion?
rationale: Tests can prove the state machine, but they cannot decide the product tradeoff between future recoverability and clearer terminal operator signaling for currently unreconcilable sends.

options.title: Accept recoverable pending
options.body: Merge after maintainer review and leave the receipt/reconciliation/user-surfacing design to the linked broader issue.

options.title: Keep terminal failure
options.body: Reject or revise this PR so no-reconciler ambiguous rows still move to failed after bounded retries while refusing blind replay.

options.title: Require operator surfacing first
options.body: Ask for an approved doctor, UI, API, or health surface for deferred ambiguous rows before changing the recovery state.

recommendation.title: Accept recoverable pending
recommendation.body: Merge after maintainer review and leave the receipt/reconciliation/user-surfacing design to the linked broader issue.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the recent merged outbound recovery rewrite and are the best available owner for the queue-state policy choice.
